name: Streetlight Manifesto
label: Victory
lede: Tomas Kalnoky walked out of Catch 22 after one album, spent the next fifteen years re-recording it, touring in a van that kept getting robbed, and fighting Victory Records until he bought his masters back.

eras.title: The kid who left Catch 22
eras.text: Tomas Kalnoky, born in Prague and raised in East Brunswick, New Jersey, fronted Catch 22 on its first album and then quit. The record he left behind, Keasbey Nights, became a third-wave ska touchstone, and he would spend years trying to take it back.

years.h: Tomas Kalnoky starts [[Catch 22|e59b17a9-2c0d-4284-854e-6d51a448091d]] in East Brunswick, New Jersey
years.p: Tomas Kalnoky, a teenager born in Prague, fronts the new ska-punk band Catch 22 on guitar and vocals.

years.h: Catch 22's Keasbey Nights, on Victory Records
years.p: Catch 22's debut, written and sung by Tomas Kalnoky with horns by Jamie Egan, becomes one of the best-known third-wave ska records.

years.h: Tomas Kalnoky quits Catch 22 right after Keasbey Nights
years.p: Rather than tour, Tomas Kalnoky leaves Catch 22 to keep studying, a choice Wikipedia says was influenced by his parents. His own page says he went to study visual art.

years.h: Bandits of the Acoustic Revolution cut A Call to Arms
years.p: Tomas Kalnoky's acoustic collective records the A Call to Arms EP, with early versions of songs he'd rework for Streetlight Manifesto.

years.h: Streetlight Manifesto forms in New Brunswick, New Jersey
years.p: Kalnoky's new band is stacked with ex-[[Catch 22|e59b17a9-2c0d-4284-854e-6d51a448091d]] players. The four-song demo includes Point/Counterpoint and We Are the Few.
years.xp: The demo line-up: Josh Ansley (bass), Jamie Egan (trombone, trumpet), Tomas Kalnoky (guitar, vocals), Stuart Karmatz (drums), Dan Ross (saxophones) and Pete Sibilia (tenor sax). Paul Lowndes replaced Karmatz and Jim Conti replaced Sibilia; before the first shows Mike Soprano joined on trombone and Chris Thatcher took over drums.

eras.title: Horns, a van and two robberies
eras.text: Streetlight's first album came out on the same label as Keasbey Nights, and the band sold out its first headline show. Then the line-up churned and thieves hit them twice in a month.

years.h: Everything Goes Numb: Streetlight's debut on Victory
years.p: Tomas Kalnoky's new band releases its first album on Victory Records, the label that put out Keasbey Nights.

years.h: Streetlight and Catch 22 take shots at each other on record
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto's debut and Catch 22's Dinosaur Sounds both come out in 2003 with what Wikipedia calls supposed veiled attacks on each other. The bands later made up; Catch 22's Kevin Gunther now books Streetlight's tours.

years.h: First headline show at Rutgers University sells out
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto headlines for the first time at Rutgers University in New Brunswick, and the show sells out.

years.h: Bassist Josh Ansley quits Streetlight to act
years.p: Josh Ansley leaves Streetlight Manifesto in September 2004 to pursue an acting career.

years.h: Jamie Egan leaves. Delano Bonner debuts at Rowan three days later
years.p: Horn player Jamie Egan quits before the Ska Is Dead 2 tour. New trumpeter Delano Bonner plays his first show January 25 at Rowan University in Glassboro, New Jersey.

years.h: Streetlight tours Europe despite visa trouble
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto makes it to Europe in April 2005 despite complications with visas.

years.h: Dan Ross leaves mid-tour. Mike Brown debuts in Baltimore
years.p: Saxophonist Dan Ross leaves mid-tour for a family crisis and later teaches math at Piscataway High School. Mike Brown plays his first US show in Baltimore on May 31.

years.h: Thieves take about $80,000 from Streetlight's van in Jacksonville
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto's van is burglarized in Jacksonville, Florida, and roughly $80,000 in instruments and merchandise is gone. Four shows are cancelled.
years.xp: A month later, in November 2005, the band was robbed again in Paris and lost its 24-track hard drive recorder.

eras.title: Re-recording the past
eras.text: Victory planned to reissue Keasbey Nights, so Kalnoky re-made it himself with Streetlight. The band's next album is the one fans rank highest, and a covers project meant to run 99 songs stopped at one volume.

q: I've always thought it sounded like pure garbage sound-wise.
years.h: Streetlight re-records Catch 22's Keasbey Nights
years.p: When Tomas Kalnoky heard Victory planned to reissue the 1998 Catch 22 album unchanged, he re-recorded it with Streetlight Manifesto on the band's own money. Victory released it in March 2006.
years.xp:
Kalnoky said he didn't want fans duped into buying a new edition of something they already had. The new version has new verses, new arrangements, and a text-to-speech interview in place of the original ending of the final track.

AllMusic gave both versions four stars but said the remake lost some of the original's raw, youthful energy.

years.h: Trumpeter Matt Stewart replaces Delano Bonner
years.p: Between December 2006 and July 2007, Delano Bonner leaves Streetlight Manifesto and Matt Stewart takes the trumpet chair.

years.h: Somewhere in the Between, sold at a show four days early
years.p: Streetlight's second album of originals reaches No. 2 on Heatseekers, and the band sells it at a show before the release date. Punknews ranks it No. 19 of the year.

years.h: Jim Conti is hospitalized with a facial infection
years.p: Saxophonist Jim Conti is hospitalized mid-tour, and Streetlight Manifesto plays shorter sets heavy on older songs.

years.h: Tomas Kalnoky breaks his arm on Warped Tour and keeps singing
years.p: Kalnoky fractures his arm during the 2009 Warped Tour. He keeps singing while another guitarist covers his parts.

years.h: 99 Songs of Revolution: Vol. 1, the only volume
years.p: Streetlight's covers project was planned as a series. As of 2026, volume one is the only one released.

eras.title: The war with Victory
eras.text: The Hands That Thieve was Streetlight's last album for Victory, and the fight over it spilled into boycotts, a leak, a lawsuit and finally a buyout of the band's own masters.

years.h: The Hands That Thieve is announced, then delayed twice
years.p: Streetlight announces its fourth album for November 6, 2012. Label conflicts and rewrites push it to January 2013, then April 30.

years.src: Wikipedia: Streetlight Manifesto · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: Streetlight asks fans to boycott Victory, even its own records
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto says Victory withheld copies of The Hands That Thieve from the band and pre-order customers, and asks fans to boycott Victory merch everywhere, including Amazon.
years.xp: The band kept taking pre-orders on its own site with no physical copies to send. Wikipedia's Victory Records page dates the boycott call to February 2012; the band page says February 2013.

years.h: Streetlight quits touring year-round
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto says it will stop touring year-round after 2013, will self-release future albums, and plays out the year on the End of the Beginning Tour.

years.h: The Toh Kay version is pulled, then leaks with a message for Victory
years.p: Kalnoky's acoustic version as Toh Kay, The Hand That Thieves, is cancelled after Victory has it removed from Amazon. It leaks on its planned release day with the metadata title "Fuck Victory".

years.h: The Hands That Thieve finally comes out
years.p: Eleven days after it leaks online, Streetlight's last Victory album is released. It reaches No. 95 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Pre-order fans get a blank CD-R and an orange cat
years.p: The mystery gift for fans who pre-ordered The Hands That Thieve from the band's store: a digipak with a blank CD-R, a 24-page booklet, and an orange tabby cat on the cover.

q: @victoryrecords hasn't paid us a cent in royalties in over 2 yrs.
years.src: Wikipedia: Streetlight Manifesto · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: Victory Records sues Tomas Kalnoky
years.p: Victory says Streetlight owes it albums, arguing a covers album and a record traded for a $10,000 emergency advance don't count. The band says the suit seeks $5 million, not $1 million.
years.xp: Victory's suit also alleged copyright infringement over The Hands That Thieve and the Toh Kay version. Early coverage reported $1,000,000; three days later the band said it was five million.

years.h: Streetlight settles with Victory and buys back its masters
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto and Victory Records announce a settlement: the band leaves the label and buys all its master recordings for an undisclosed sum.

eras.title: The album that keeps not coming out
eras.text: Streetlight announced a sixth album in 2021 and has been circling it since. Along the way the band lost trumpeter Matt Stewart.

years.h: Streetlight promises a new album for 2022
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto announces a sixth studio album for sometime in 2022. By early 2023 the band says progress is slow.

years.h: A new song, Mayday, at the Starland Ballroom
years.p: On The Calm Before The Chaos Tour, Streetlight teases a new song, Mayday, at the Starland Ballroom in Sayreville, New Jersey.

years.h: Trumpeter Matt Stewart dies at 41
years.p: Matt Stewart, in Streetlight Manifesto since 2007, died September 10, 2023. Mike Soprano returned for San Francisco and Los Angeles, then Joshua Gawel of Lucky Chops took over.

yt: The Place Behind the Stars teaser
years.h: The Place Behind the Stars is set for June 24
years.p: After a teaser on April 3, Streetlight announces its sixth album for June 24, 2025.

years.h: The Place Behind the Stars is postponed indefinitely
years.p: Eight days before release Streetlight pulls the date. On June 24 it posts three songs to YouTube as pre-release mixes.
